newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends off sharply, Feb breaks support.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends off sharply, Feb breaks support.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, with cratering cash prices amid mild weather forecasts driving February through support, industry sources said.
February skidded 15.4 cents to close at $2.916 per million British thermal units, below psychological support at $3. March settled 14.2 cents lower at $2.632.

"The forecast doesn't look good (for the bulls), and the lack of weather means more downside ahead," said one East Coast trader, noting Gulf Coast cash prices have cratered about 30 percent since late last week.

Despite expectations for the largest weekly stock draw of the heating season in Wednesday's AGA report, traders said forecasts for above- to much-above-normal U.S. temperatures later this week and next have undermined sentiment.

Early withdrawal estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report range from 150 to 225 bcf. Last year, stocks feel by 105 bcf, meaning a draw in the expected range will reduce the surplus to 1996.

Chart traders said February's close below the $3 level turned the technical picture decidedly bearish. They pegged next support at the Dec 31 low of $2.613. Resistance was seen at $3.33, $3.64 and then in the $3.80-3.84 area.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices tumbled 25 cents Tuesday to the mid-$2.90s. Midcontinent prices were down slightly to the mid-to-high $2.80s. Gas at the New York city gate skidded 50-75 cents to the $3.50s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip fell by 6.7 cents to $2.295. NYMEX said an estimated 45,229 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 38,036.
NYMEX February Henry Hub natgas expires next Monday.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, February closed 14 cents lower at $2.79, while deferreds finished down by 3.5 to 14.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.4 cents to 12.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 412 contracts traded, up from Monday's total of 160.
